value.body: Between landing and the next take-off, many teams work on an aircraft at once — baggage and cargo loaders, fuellers, caterers, cleaners and engineers. A ground operations executive coordinates them so the flight leaves on time and safely, and prepares documents such as load sheets. Employers are airlines and ground-handling companies at airports.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate; aviation-management degrees and diplomas are common
items.note: Some posts accept Class 12 with aviation training

items.label: Workplace
items.value: Airport ramp and operations control rooms

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Rotating shifts, including nights and holidays

items.label: Domestic air passengers
items.note: Passengers carried by domestic airlines, Jan–Dec 2024; ~6% above 2023

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join airlines or ground-handling companies as ground staff or operations trainees through their own recruitment drives. An airport entry pass needs a background check, and a medical and English test are common.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: duty manager, load controller, station manager.
Work is outdoors on the ramp in heat, rain and noise for part of the shift.
Airline schedules and staffing change with traffic and seasons.
